parsed.attack: On-device inference makes this free to run, and that is exactly the problem: with zero marginal cost and a hard three-person wedge there is nothing to meter, so the paywall must be artificial (a fourth contact), the weakest upsell in consumer software. The category also prices below the entire median payer band - relationship-reminder apps sell at $2.99-4.99/month, netting $2.54-4.24, against a $8-24 median. At their own 3% conversion kill line, iOS costs $195 per paying user and Android $64; at $3.40 net that is 57 months and 19 months of payback on a product whose success condition is that it stays silent and produces nothing on most days, which is the worst possible retention signal for a subscription the user is asked to keep renewing.
parsed.strongest_defence: Zero COGS means the only cost is the developer's time, and community_embed into an enormous audience (adult children of ageing parents is tens of millions) needs only a fraction of a percent to organically install; a lifetime unlock at $19.99 sidesteps the subscription-renewal problem entirely and still nets $17 per buyer at zero marginal cost.
parsed.verdict_reason: Margin is genuinely free, but the price the category supports sits below the median payer band and paid acquisition needs 19-57 months of payback, so the idea rests entirely on unpaid community distribution and an artificial paywall.
